In [[geometry]], the '''gyroelongated bicupolae''' are an infinite sets of [[Polyhedron|polyhedra]], constructed by adjoining two ''n''-gonal [[cupola (geometry)|cupola]]s to an ''n''-gonal [[antiprism]]. The triangular, square, and pentagonal gyroelongated bicupola are three of five [[Johnson solid]]s which are [[chirality (mathematics)|chiral]], meaning that they have a "left-handed" and a "right-handed" form.

Adjoining two [[triangular prism]]s to a square antiprism also generates a polyhedron, but not a Johnson solid, as it is not convex. The hexagonal form is also a polygon, but has [[coplanar]] faces. Higher forms can be constructed without regular faces.
